newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cashpoints drained to prevent robbery.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cashpoints drained to prevent robbery.

text.p: Some of Belgium's 1,130 hole-in-the-wall electronic cashpoints are being drained of money and shut down, while cash levels at others are being cut back, to discourage robbers from blasting them open.

After three successful and one failed raid in which explosives were used to blow the machines from their concrete mountings, operator Banksys said cashpoints in dangerous locations would be starved of cash.
In one spectacular heist five million Belgian francs ($156,000) was stolen this week from a Banque Bruxelles Lambert cashpoint near Brussels.
Instead of withdrawing cash, users would be encouraged to pay with their credit or debit cards, Banksys spokesman Jo Deglin told Belgian radio.
He gave no exact details of the locations considered to be dangerous -- some of them are near motorways -- noor the number of machines to be shut down.

Other cashpoints would contain only enough cash to meet one day and one night's demand, while others still would be left without money during the night. Deglin gave no percentages for the three categories of measures.
"We must avoid situations where there is more money in the machines than is needed...they will just have to be re-stocked more frequently," the Banksys spokesman said.
